sentence: The old swimming pool has become a community center. Local apprentices converted it last year.
setupText: Choose the continuation keeping the pool as grammatical subject and retaining the named builders.
taskText: The old swimming pool has become a community center. Local apprentices converted it last year.
text: Choose the continuation keeping the pool as grammatical subject and retaining the named builders. The old swimming pool has become a community center. Local apprentices converted it last year.
options: It was converted by local apprentices last year.
The pool was converted last year.
Local apprentices converted the pool last year.
Local apprentices were trained during last year's conversion.
answer: It was converted by local apprentices last year.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2341:Topic continuity with an explicitly retained passive agent
explanation: It keeps the pool as the topic; by local apprentices preserves the supplied agent. Passive voice need not hide who acted.

This keeps the pool as subject but drops the builders, which the task requires you to retain.
rationales.Local apprentices converted the pool las: This preserves the event but makes the apprentices, not the pool, the grammatical subject.
rationales.It was converted by local apprentices la: It keeps the pool as the topic; by local apprentices preserves the supplied agent. Passive voice need not hide who acted.
rationales.Local apprentices were trained during la: This adds a training event that the source does not state and makes the apprentices the subject.

sentence: The water samples ___ on Tuesday and ___ for contamination, so the results are ready.
setupText: Choose the pair reporting collection at a finished past time and completed testing relevant now.
taskText: The water samples ___ on Tuesday and ___ for contamination, so the results are ready.
text: Choose the pair reporting collection at a finished past time and completed testing relevant now. The water samples ___ on Tuesday and ___ for contamination, so the results are ready.
options: have collected / tested
were collected / have been tested
were collecting / have tested
have been collected / were testing
answer: were collected / have been tested
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2342:Different tense anchors in coordinated passive events
explanation: Were collected dates the past sampling; have been tested reports completed testing with results now. Both keep samples as receivers.

rationales.were collected / have been tested: Were collected dates the past sampling; have been tested reports completed testing with results now. Both keep samples as receivers.
rationales.have collected / tested: Have collected makes the samples collect something, and tested without an auxiliary remains active in this coordination.
rationales.were collecting / have tested: Both active forms give samples the role of workers rather than things collected and tested.
rationales.have been collected / were testing: Have been collected does not fit the dated event in this ordinary report, and were testing makes the samples active testers.

sentence: The temporary seating collapsed during rehearsal. It ___ before anyone used it.
setupText: Choose the form expressing a missed obligation before the event.
taskText: The temporary seating collapsed during rehearsal. It ___ before anyone used it.
text: Choose the form expressing a missed obligation before the event. The temporary seating collapsed during rehearsal. It ___ before anyone used it.
options: should inspect
should be inspecting
should have inspected
should have been inspected
answer: should have been inspected
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2343:Modal perfect passive for retrospective criticism
explanation: 'Should have been inspected' says the seating ought to have received inspection before use; the criticism concerns an earlier unmet obligation.

rationales.should inspect: Should inspect makes the seating the inspector and gives a current recommendation rather than a missed earlier obligation.
rationales.should have been inspected: 'Should have been inspected' says the seating ought to have received inspection before use; the criticism concerns an earlier unmet obligation.
rationales.should be inspecting: Should be inspecting is active progressive and makes the seating the inspecting agent.
rationales.should have inspected: Should have inspected is active perfect and assigns the inspection to the seating rather than to people checking it.

sentence: The shared calendar is empty. Accidental deletion is one possible explanation, but it has not been confirmed.
setupText: Choose the statement preserving uncertainty about an earlier accidental deletion.
taskText: The shared calendar is empty. Accidental deletion is one possible explanation, but it has not been confirmed.
text: Choose the statement preserving uncertainty about an earlier accidental deletion. The shared calendar is empty. Accidental deletion is one possible explanation, but it has not been confirmed.
options: The entries may have been deleted accidentally.
The entries must have been deleted accidentally.
The entries were deleted accidentally.
The entries cannot have been deleted accidentally.
answer: The entries may have been deleted accidentally.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2344:Uncertain earlier event in a modal perfect passive
explanation: May have been deleted combines possibility, earlier time, and passive voice without claiming the explanation is verified.

rationales.The entries must have been deleted accid: Must have presents a strong conclusion rather than the stated unconfirmed possibility among explanations.
The simple past passive asserts the deletion as a fact, exceeding the evidence.
rationales.The entries cannot have been deleted acc: Cannot have rules deletion out, reversing its status as a possible explanation.
rationales.The entries may have been deleted accide: May have been deleted combines possibility, earlier time, and passive voice without claiming the explanation is verified.

sentence: Temporary access codes are confidential. Staff are prohibited from including them in public notices.
setupText: Choose the rule that makes disclosure forbidden rather than optional.
taskText: Temporary access codes are confidential. Staff are prohibited from including them in public notices.
text: Choose the rule that makes disclosure forbidden rather than optional. Temporary access codes are confidential. Staff are prohibited from including them in public notices.
options: The codes need not be included in public notices.
The codes must not be included in public notices.
The codes may be included in public notices.
The codes should have been included in public notices.
answer: The codes must not be included in public notices.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2345:Prohibition versus lack of obligation in passive rules
explanation: 'Must not be included' expresses the prohibition while keeping the confidential codes as the topic.

rationales.The codes need not be included in public: Need not removes an obligation but does not prohibit inclusion.
rationales.The codes must not be included in public: 'Must not be included' expresses the prohibition while keeping the confidential codes as the topic.
rationales.The codes may be included in public noti: May be included gives permission, contrary to the rule.
rationales.The codes should have been included in p: Should have been included recommends an earlier action rather than forbidding disclosure.

sentence: Several historians think the tunnel once connected the two houses. No one has verified the connection.
setupText: Choose the statement reporting a belief without upgrading it to proof.
taskText: Several historians think the tunnel once connected the two houses. No one has verified the connection.
text: Choose the statement reporting a belief without upgrading it to proof. Several historians think the tunnel once connected the two houses. No one has verified the connection.
options: The tunnel is known to have connected the two houses.
The tunnel is proved to have connected the two houses.
The tunnel has been shown to have connected the two houses.
The tunnel is believed to have connected the two houses.
answer: The tunnel is believed to have connected the two houses.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2346:Reporting passive preserving belief rather than verified knowledge
explanation: Is believed to attributes the connection to a belief; the perfect infinitive places the supposed connection earlier.

rationales.The tunnel is believed to have connected: Is believed to attributes the connection to a belief; the perfect infinitive places the supposed connection earlier.
rationales.The tunnel is known to have connected th: Is known to presents the connection as established knowledge, beyond the source.
rationales.The tunnel is proved to have connected t: Is proved to claims proof, which the source explicitly lacks.
rationales.The tunnel has been shown to have connec: Has been shown to claims that evidence has demonstrated the connection, not merely that historians think it existed.

sentence: People say that the mineral spring is unusually warm.
setupText: Choose the impersonal passive report that preserves a current general claim.
taskText: People say that the mineral spring is unusually warm.
text: Choose the impersonal passive report that preserves a current general claim. People say that the mineral spring is unusually warm.
options: It is said the mineral spring to be unusually warm.
The mineral spring is said that it is unusually warm.
It is said that the mineral spring is unusually warm.
It says that the mineral spring is unusually warm.
answer: It is said that the mineral spring is unusually warm.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2347:Impersonal reporting passive with a that clause
explanation: It is said that provides an impersonal reporting passive while retaining the original claim about the spring.

rationales.It is said the mineral spring to be unus: This mixes the impersonal it construction with the infinitive pattern; use it is said that plus a finite clause.
rationales.The mineral spring is said that it is un: With the spring as subject, use 'is said to be'; the impersonal that-clause pattern instead begins 'it is said'.
rationales.It is said that the mineral spring is un: It is said that provides an impersonal reporting passive while retaining the original claim about the spring.
rationales.It says that the mineral spring is unusu: It says is active and would require it to refer to a source, such as a guidebook; it is not the requested impersonal passive.

sentence: The newspaper currently reports an unverified belief that someone stole the medal before the exhibition opened.
setupText: Choose the current reporting passive with the medal as grammatical subject and the theft explicitly earlier than the belief.
taskText: The newspaper currently reports an unverified belief that someone stole the medal before the exhibition opened.
text: Choose the current reporting passive with the medal as grammatical subject and the theft explicitly earlier than the belief. The newspaper currently reports an unverified belief that someone stole the medal before the exhibition opened.
options: Someone is believed to have stolen the medal.
The medal is believed to be stolen.
The medal is believed to have been stolen.
The medal was believed to have been stolen.
answer: The medal is believed to have been stolen.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2348:Earlier passive event inside a personal reporting construction
explanation: Is believed gives the current reporting frame, and to have been stolen explicitly places the medal's theft before that belief.

rationales.Someone is believed to have stolen the m: This reports the same kind of earlier event but makes someone, not the medal, the grammatical subject.
To be stolen can describe an expected event or a supposed current state; it does not explicitly mark the theft as earlier than the current belief.
rationales.The medal was believed to have been stol: 'Was believed' locates the reporting belief in the past rather than the current belief requested.
rationales.The medal is believed to have been stole: Is believed gives the current reporting frame, and to have been stolen explicitly places the medal's theft before that belief.

sentence: The trainee got dismissed during the restructuring. The account gives no reason for choosing that employee.
setupText: Choose what the get-passive establishes without assigning blame.
taskText: The trainee got dismissed during the restructuring. The account gives no reason for choosing that employee.
text: Choose what the get-passive establishes without assigning blame. The trainee got dismissed during the restructuring. The account gives no reason for choosing that employee.
options: The trainee deliberately arranged to be dismissed.
The trainee dismissed the person leading the restructuring.
The trainee's misconduct was the reason for the dismissal.
The trainee was dismissed; got does not by itself establish fault or intention.
answer: The trainee was dismissed; got does not by itself establish fault or intention.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2349:Get-passive without inferred responsibility
explanation: Got dismissed presents the trainee as undergoing dismissal; responsibility, intention, and the reason require additional evidence.

rationales.The trainee deliberately arranged to be: A get-passive does not by itself mean the subject planned or arranged the event.
rationales.The trainee was dismissed; got does not: Got dismissed presents the trainee as undergoing dismissal; responsibility, intention, and the reason require additional evidence.
rationales.The trainee dismissed the person leading: This reverses the trainee's role from dismissed employee to dismissing agent.
rationales.The trainee's misconduct was the reason: No misconduct is stated, and the get-passive alone cannot supply it.

sentence: The account must identify a guard performing the locking.
setupText: Choose the sentence that explicitly presents a locking action rather than just a continuing state.
taskText: The account must identify a guard performing the locking.
text: Choose the sentence that explicitly presents a locking action rather than just a continuing state. The account must identify a guard performing the locking.
options: The storeroom was locked by the guard at midnight.
The storeroom remained locked overnight.
The storeroom was still locked at dawn.
The storeroom seemed securely locked.
answer: The storeroom was locked by the guard at midnight.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2350:Event passive distinguished from a participial state description
explanation: By the guard identifies an agent and at midnight locates the locking event, giving the requested action reading.

'Remained locked' describes a continuing state without reporting the guard's action.
'Still locked' describes the state at dawn, not who performed the locking.
rationales.The storeroom was locked by the guard at: By the guard identifies an agent and at midnight locates the locking event, giving the requested action reading.
Seemed securely locked reports an apparent state rather than a locking event by a guard.

sentence: The bed looks freshly made, but it has clearly ___.
setupText: Choose the passive completion preserving the meaning someone slept in the bed.
taskText: The bed looks freshly made, but it has clearly ___.
text: Choose the passive completion preserving the meaning someone slept in the bed. The bed looks freshly made, but it has clearly ___.
options: been slept
being slept in
been sleeping
been slept in
answer: been slept in
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2351:Prepositional passive retaining in
explanation: Been slept in retains in from sleep in and makes the bed the location affected by someone's use.

rationales.been slept in: Been slept in retains in from sleep in and makes the bed the location affected by someone's use.
rationales.been slept: Dropping in loses the required relation between sleeping and the bed.
rationales.being slept in: After has, the passive perfect needs been rather than being.
rationales.been sleeping: Been sleeping is active perfect continuous; it makes the bed the sleeper.

sentence: The agency reserved a seat for the traveler.
setupText: Choose the passive paraphrase preserving the traveler as beneficiary and the agency as actor.
taskText: The agency reserved a seat for the traveler.
text: Choose the passive paraphrase preserving the traveler as beneficiary and the agency as actor. The agency reserved a seat for the traveler.
options: A seat was reserved by the traveler for the agency.
A seat was reserved for the traveler by the agency.
The agency was reserved a seat by the traveler.
The traveler was reserved for a seat by the agency.
answer: A seat was reserved for the traveler by the agency.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2352:Preserving beneficiary and agent in a passive transfer
explanation: For the traveler preserves the beneficiary; by the agency preserves the agent, with the seat as passive subject.

rationales.A seat was reserved by the traveler for: This exchanges the beneficiary and the reserving agent.
rationales.The agency was reserved a seat by the tr: This also makes the agency receive the reservation and the traveler perform it.
rationales.The traveler was reserved for a seat by: This makes the traveler the thing reserved rather than the person benefiting from the seat reservation.
rationales.A seat was reserved for the traveler by: For the traveler preserves the beneficiary; by the agency preserves the agent, with the seat as passive subject.

sentence: The members elected Dr. Bell chair of the association.
setupText: Choose the sentence preserving 'chair' as the role the members elected the candidate to fill.
taskText: The members elected Dr. Bell chair of the association.
text: Choose the sentence preserving 'chair' as the role the members elected the candidate to fill. The members elected Dr. Bell chair of the association.
options: Dr. Bell elected the chair of the association.
Dr. Bell was elected by the chair of the association.
Dr. Bell was elected chair of the association.
The chair elected Dr. Bell to the association.
answer: Dr. Bell was elected chair of the association.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2353:Retained object complement after passive promotion
explanation: 'Was elected' is passive, and 'chair' remains the complement naming the role Dr. Bell receives.

rationales.Dr. Bell elected the chair of the associ: This makes Dr. Bell the voter instead of the person elected.
rationales.Dr. Bell was elected by the chair of the: 'By the chair' turns 'chair' into the electing agent rather than the role awarded.
rationales.Dr. Bell was elected chair of the associ: 'Was elected' is passive, and 'chair' remains the complement naming the role Dr. Bell receives.
rationales.The chair elected Dr. Bell to the associ: This changes both the electing agent and the role into mere association membership.

sentence: Goods manufactured locally usually arrive within two days.

answer: Goods that are manufactured locally
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2354:Expanding a reduced passive relative clause
explanation: 'Manufactured locally' is a reduced passive relative clause meaning 'goods that are manufactured locally'.

rationales.Goods that manufacture local products: This makes the goods manufacture other products and changes the description.
rationales.Goods that are manufactured locally: 'Manufactured locally' is a reduced passive relative clause meaning 'goods that are manufactured locally'.
rationales.Goods that are manufacturing locally: Are manufacturing is active progressive and gives goods the role of manufacturers.
rationales.Goods that have manufactured locally: Have manufactured is active perfect, again making goods the producers rather than their products.

sentence: Revise: 'After being heated for ten minutes, the technician weighed the sample.'
setupText: Choose the revision making the sample, not the technician, the thing heated.
taskText: Revise: 'After being heated for ten minutes, the technician weighed the sample.'
text: Choose the revision making the sample, not the technician, the thing heated. Revise: 'After being heated for ten minutes, the technician weighed the sample.'
options: After being heated for ten minutes, the technician was weighed with the sample.
After heating for ten minutes, the sample weighed the technician.
After being heated for ten minutes, the sample was weighed by the technician.
After being heated for ten minutes, the technician weighed more carefully.
answer: After being heated for ten minutes, the sample was weighed by the technician.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2355:Subject control of an introductory passive participle clause
explanation: The subject the sample now matches the understood receiver of being heated, and the technician remains the person weighing it.

rationales.After being heated for ten minutes, the: The subject the sample now matches the understood receiver of being heated, and the technician remains the person weighing it.
The technician is still the subject understood as heated and is now also made the receiver of weighing.
rationales.After heating for ten minutes, the sampl: This makes the sample an active weigher and reverses the measurement relationship.
rationales.After being heated for ten minutes, the: The added adverb does not fix the attachment: the opening still points to the technician as the heated subject.

sentence: This fabric washes well, even in cold water.
setupText: Choose the analysis of this product description.
taskText: This fabric washes well, even in cold water.
text: Choose the analysis of this product description. This fabric washes well, even in cold water.
options: The active form describes how readily people can wash the fabric.
The fabric is described as actively washing other materials.
The sentence reports a particular wash that has already finished.
The fabric is being washed at the moment of speaking.
answer: The active form describes how readily people can wash the fabric.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2356:Middle construction distinguished from active agency and event passive
explanation: This middle construction uses an active form to describe a property of something people act on; it is not morphologically a be-passive.

rationales.The fabric is described as actively wash: In this use, the fabric is understood as the thing washed, not as a washing agent.
rationales.The sentence reports a particular wash t: The present statement describes a general property, not a dated completed wash.
rationales.The fabric is being washed at the moment: It is a property statement, not a present continuous passive reporting an action underway.
rationales.The active form describes how readily pe: This middle construction uses an active form to describe a property of something people act on; it is not morphologically a be-passive.

sentence: During the storm, our neighbors had their fence damaged by falling debris.
setupText: Choose the reading licensed by the accidental-event context.
taskText: During the storm, our neighbors had their fence damaged by falling debris.

The neighbors experienced damage to their fence.
The neighbors damaged someone else's fence.
The neighbors finished repairing the fence before the storm.
answer: The neighbors experienced damage to their fence.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2357:Adverse have-object-participle construction versus arranged service
explanation: Had their fence damaged presents an event affecting their property, with falling debris as the stated cause.

rationales.The neighbors arranged for workers to da: 'Have an object damaged' can describe an unwanted experience; this storm context does not support a commissioned service.
rationales.The neighbors experienced damage to thei: Had their fence damaged presents an event affecting their property, with falling debris as the stated cause.
rationales.The neighbors damaged someone else's fen: The fence belongs to the neighbors, and they are not identified as the damaging agents.
rationales.The neighbors finished repairing the fen: The clause concerns damage during the storm, not a completed earlier repair.

taskText: An officer saw the visitor enter the courtyard.

The visitor was seen to enter the courtyard.
answer: The visitor was seen to enter the courtyard.

explanation: 'Was seen to enter' preserves the visitor as the observed person; the passive restores 'to' before the infinitive.

rationales.The visitor was seen enter the courtyard: The passive counterpart of saw the visitor enter uses to enter in standard English.
rationales.The visitor was seen to entering the cou: After 'to' here, use the base form 'enter', not 'entering'.
rationales.The visitor was seen to enter the courty: 'Was seen to enter' preserves the visitor as the observed person; the passive restores 'to' before the infinitive.
rationales.The visitor was seeing the officer enter: This makes the visitor the observer and the officer the person entering, reversing the original roles.

In the passive of make someone do something, use be made to do it; the staff remain the people compelled to wait.

sentence: A traffic update says, 'The eastbound lane is being resurfaced.' The road authority knows which contractor is working there.
setupText: Choose the inference justified by the omission of the contractor's name.
taskText: A traffic update says, 'The eastbound lane is being resurfaced.' The road authority knows which contractor is working there.
text: Choose the inference justified by the omission of the contractor's name. A traffic update says, 'The eastbound lane is being resurfaced.' The road authority knows which contractor is working there.
options: The writer has proved that no contractor is involved.
The writer cannot know who is carrying out the work.
The update can foreground the affected lane without naming a known contractor.
The passive implies that the road authority is concealing misconduct.
answer: The update can foreground the affected lane without naming a known contractor.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-b2-2360:Known-agent omission driven by information relevance
explanation: Agent omission can serve the update's focus on traffic conditions even when the agent is known.

rationales.The writer has proved that no contractor: Omitting the contractor does not deny that someone is performing the work.
rationales.The writer cannot know who is carrying o: The context explicitly says the authority knows the contractor; a passive need not indicate ignorance.
rationales.The passive implies that the road author: Passive form alone provides no evidence of concealment or misconduct.
rationales.The update can foreground the affected l: Agent omission can serve the update's focus on traffic conditions even when the agent is known.
